Overall, estimates of kink wave energy density and scaling laws provide observational constraints on the importance of the proposed kink wave heating mechanism, with the current preliminary results suggesting that the uniturbulent kink wave heating may be a significant source of energy and heat in coronal loops.

papers.title: Calibrating the cosmic distance ladder for independent dark energy constraints
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological results presented by the DESI collaboration show a clear deviation from the $\Lambda$CDM model when considering a time-dependent dark energy equation of state. This deviation is strongly driven by the SNe Ia surveys, which all share the same low redshift sample. The ZTF survey provides the current larger SNe Ia sample at low redshift, which will significantly increase the constraining power. In this context, the LEMAITRE collaboration aims to provide new constraints on dark energy parameters using three independent SNe Ia datasets: ZTF, SNLS and HSC. This effort requires robust photometric calibration, with a particular focus on filter transmission measurement and star catalog calibration. The target for LEMAITRE is to control the calibration systematics on distance moduli below 0.4%.
authors: Enya Van den Abeele (on behalf of the LEMAITRE project)

papers.title: The LEMAITRE project: An Independent Probe of the $w-w_a$ Tension
papers.abstract: Recent BAO, CMB, and Type Ia supernova constraints on the dark-energy equation of state show a tension with the cosmological-constant model at the heart of $\Lambda$CDM, partly driven by low-redshift supernova measurements. We present the LEMAITRE project, a new measurement of the dark energy equation of state, based on a distinct SN~Ia dataset (2800 from ZTF, 170 from SNLS and 300 from HSC), a dedicated calibration program, and a new, independent analysis pipeline.
authors: Nicolas Regnault (on behalf of the LEMAITRE project)

papers.title: Cardinal RG=GR: Phase-Space Cardinality and the Cosmological Constant and Hierarchy Problems
papers.abstract: The effective field theory approach constructs the low-energy theory by integrating out fluctuations above an ultraviolet scale which raises the cosmological constant and hierarchy problems. We investigate an alternative prescription in which the quantum theory is restricted to a finite accessible region of phase space, characterized by a dimensionless cardinality $\mathcal N$, rather than by independently prescribed spacetime and momentum scales. At fixed cardinality these scales are related. For Euclidean de Sitter space, the stationarity condition for the gravitational action can then be written as a stationarity condition with respect to the momentum scale, a relation which we call Cardinal RG=GR. We demonstrate the relation between $\mathcal N$ and the Gibbons-Hawking entropy of de Sitter space, compute the cosmological constant proportional to ${1}/{\sqrt{\mathcal N}}$, show that it is radiatively stable and apply the same prescription to demonstrate the radiative stability of the mass parameter for a simple interacting scalar field model, thereby illuminating the resolution of the hierarchy problem. We also establish a precise limit, involving gravitational data, in which the conventional results of Quantum Field Theory and the Renormalization Group are recovered.

papers.title: From a mass invariant in a gravo-turbulent medium to the characteristic mass of the star-forming cores
papers.abstract: The origin of the observed universality, or, say, the limited variations, of the stellar initial mass function (IMF) and its precursor, the prestellar core mass function (CMF), and thus of the characteristic mass of stars and cores, across a wide range of different galactic environments remains an open, fundamental problem in astrophysics. In this paper, we demonstrate that we can explain this property from gravity and turbulence only, using a mass time-invariant that remains valid for a broad class of turbulent flows throughout the star formation process. This mass invariant is entirely determined by the large-scale normalisation of the field of density fluctuations in the Galactic Interstellar Medium (ISM), induced by turbulence. Using high-resolution numerical simulations, we first verify that the temporal invariance of this quantity is preserved in a self-gravitating turbulent medium. Then, introducing a self-consistent model of the statistical properties of the density field in the self-gravitating multiphase turbulent ISM, we show that the universality of the characteristic mass of star-forming cores is imposed by this invariant together with the scaling of the Larson relations. Our model successfully predicts the characteristic mass of the cores in Milky Way-like star-forming regions, as well as in more extreme environments such as high-mass star-forming regions and massive early-type galaxies. This scenario suggests that the characteristic mass of the CMF, and then probably the characteristic stellar mass, originates from a universal, fundamental property of turbulence and is imprinted both by the very early stages of the star formation process in the gravo-turbulent interstellar medium, when the dynamics of the medium are still dominated by turbulence, and by the statistical properties of small-scale self-gravitating structures.

papers.title: Log-periodic radiation cores and light rings in pure quadratic bulk gravity
papers.abstract: In the pure quadratic model of the B\"ohmer--Jensko bulk--boundary formulation of gravity, every static metric with a regular centre has vanishing central density and pressure, so no affine equation of state admits a regular non-vacuum star. We therefore study singular cores, in scale-invariant variables in which the isotropy condition is a single autonomous relation between two functions. Closures that keep the self-similar solutions as equilibria fix the stability of two vacuum lines but leave that of the matter-bearing equilibria undetermined, except at one unphysical point, so only an equation of state yields definite dynamics. For a linear equation of state the closed system has a focus, a saddle, and a vacuum point with nonzero bulk scalar that exchanges stability with the saddle in a transcritical bifurcation. At the radiation value the system is integrable, through the Tolman integral and scale invariance, and the focus becomes a nonlinear centre surrounded by log-periodic solutions. Radiation is also exactly where the line containing the matter-bearing equilibria of this closure coincides with the line of circular null orbits. Consequently every periodic radiation core with monotonic areal radius has exactly one stable and one unstable light ring per period, at radii forming two interlaced geometric progressions towards the centre with a common ratio tending to 2.165 for small oscillations. In the optical geometry the self-similar solution is a cylinder and each core a periodic tube, whose bulges and necks carry these rings. MIT bag-model configurations whose cores approach these orbits inherit this structure.

papers.title: NNLO QCD corrections to radiative and hadronic $(1S)$ decays
papers.abstract: We present the complete next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD corrections to radiative and inclusive hadronic $\Upsilon(1S)$ decays in the color-singlet framework at leading order in the heavy-quark velocity expansion. For radiative decay, the NNLO correction reshapes the photon energy spectrum and lowers the partial width in the fiducial window $0.65\leq 2E_\gamma/M_\Upsilon\leq0.92$, bringing the central prediction into good agreement with reconstructed CLEO data. For inclusive hadronic decay, the NNLO correction provides a large negative shift that lowers the predicted width from its inflated NLO value to a level fully consistent with the experimental determination. Although both individual decay widths exhibit larger renormalization-scale uncertainties at NNLO, their ratio demonstrates a significantly reduced scale dependence due to the cancellation of common short-distance dynamics and the nonperturbative matrix element. Using the window ratio inferred from CLEO measurements, we extract the strong coupling constant $\alpha_s^{(5)}(M_Z) = 0.12135^{+0.0039}_{-0.0036}$, compatible with the world average, and evaluate the sensitivity to uncalculated higher orders via the unexpanded quotient.

papers.title: Periodicities of small regular jet deviations in SS433 and their origin
papers.abstract: Based on the results of spectroscopic observations of SS433 conducted with the 2.5-m telescope at the Caucasian Mountain Observatory between 2020 and 2026, we study the deviations of the moving hydrogen and helium emission lines from their positions as predicted by the kinematic model of the jets' precessional motion. In these deviations, in addition to the previously known periodicities of $13^d.08$, $11^d.27$, $6^d.29$, and $5^d.83$, a new period of $3^d.08$ is identified. All observed periodicities are explained by a model in which the jet offsets occur in a fixed direction relative to the star-disk axis $\bf r$, and the magnitude of the offset is a function $a(\mu)$, where $\mu$ is the cosine of the angle between $\bf r$ and the direction of each jet. The odd terms of the power series expansion of $a(\mu)$ in $\mu$ yield periodicities of $6^d.29$, $5^d.83$, and $3^d.08$, with the jets shifting in opposite directions while remaining parallel. The even powers yield periodicities of $13^d.08$, $11^d.27$, and $4^d.14$ (the latter is not observed), with both jets shifting in the same direction, which was previously misinterpreted as a change in the jets' total velocity $\beta$. With the exception of the $6^d.29$ periodicity, all other displacements occur at an angle of $\approx120^\circ$ to $\bf r$. Superimposed on the regular variability are random deviations (jitter) in the jet directions, independent for the two jets, with $\sigma\lesssim1.\!\!^\circ5$.

papers.title: Equilibrium relativistic spin magnetohydrodynamics from chiral kinetic theory
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic and thermodynamically consistent framework for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics of massless chiral fermions, directly from first-order chiral kinetic theory. Starting from the covariant Wigner function, we recast the chiral kinetic equation as a pure streaming equation on a magnetically shifted mass shell, incorporating both the magnetic-moment energy and the Berry-curvature phase-space measure. This formulation yields a kinetic $H$-theorem and an entropy current with vanishing divergence in global equilibrium. We construct the equilibrium distribution for an arbitrary spin frame and derive the associated currents, energy--momentum tensor, spin tensor, entropy current, and frame-independent spin polarization, including the magnetic splitting between particles and antiparticles. Thermodynamic consistency further determines the second-order magnetovortical responses, revealing a relativistic Barnett magnetization, a temperature- and chemical-potential-independent anomalous charge density, and rotation-induced density corrections that reproduce exact field-theory results. Our framework provides a unified microscopic foundation for relativistic equilibrium spin magnetohydrodynamics and establishes a direct link between quantum kinetic theory, spin polarization, magnetization, and anomalous transport.

papers.title: Galaxy Bias and Soft Limits from Inflation
papers.abstract: Primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) leaves an imprint on large-scale structure through a scale-dependent galaxy bias, and properly incorporating the effects of higher order PNG into the bias expansion requires a consistent renormalization framework that extends beyond the squeezed limit of the bispectrum. We develop the multi-loop renormalization of bias operators in the presence of non-vanishing primordial n-point functions of arbitrary order, including stochastic contributions. We show that galaxy bias renormalization is determined by the multi-soft limits of primordial correlators and bias kernels. We provide explicit computations for one- and two-loop renormalization of deterministic operators up to fifth order in the bias expansion. Finally, we derive the renormalization group equations for the bias parameters at one and two loops.

papers.title: SlotFlow-GB: A Neural Framework for Trans-Dimensional Inference of Overlapping Galactic Binaries
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe the millihertz gravitational-wave sky, including millions of long-lived Galactic binaries (GBs), tens of thousands of which are expected to be individually resolvable throughout the mission's lifetime. Extracting these sources requires jointly determining their number and physical parameters from strongly overlapping signals, posing a computationally demanding trans-dimensional inference problem. We introduce SlotFlow-GB, a neural framework that constructs a learned approximation to the trans-dimensional posterior, producing a probability distribution over source multiplicity and parameter densities for individual binaries in a single evaluation, without requiring their number to be specified in advance. We demonstrate this framework using year-long LISA simulations containing up to ten binaries within a 2 $\mu$Hz frequency interval, focusing on a high-SNR regime in which source overlap, rather than individual-source detectability, is the primary challenge. The inferred source count differs from the true count by at most one in 94% of cases, while the model identifies individual binaries even when their signals overlap strongly in frequency. A complete evaluation, including parameter sampling, takes just 41 ms per band on one NVIDIA GH200 GPU, or 530 ms on eight laptop CPU threads. We further demonstrate that these distributions can be used to initialize subsequent likelihood-based inference, connecting fast amortized predictions with joint parameter estimation.

papers.title: Strong Field Tidal Disruptions of Rotating Stars by Spinning Black Holes
papers.abstract: We study tidal disruptions of rotating solar-type stars by a rapidly spinning supermassive black hole with general-relativistic smoothed-particle hydrodynamics. To capture strong-field effects, we place the pericentre at a few gravitational radii of a black hole, and compare with weak-field encounters at a larger pericentre around a lighter black hole. We vary the black hole spin, the orbital inclination and the stellar rotation, using rigidly and differentially rotating stars with spin aligned, anti-aligned or perpendicular to the orbital angular momentum. In the strong field, the black hole spin decides whether a core survives on equatorial and inclined orbits, and stellar rotation reduces the surviving core in every partial disruption. At the larger pericentre, as in Newtonian studies, anti-aligned rotation instead protects the star from disruption. In both cases the tide reverses an anti-aligned spin just before pericentre. The outcome differs because in the strong field the tide keeps acting on the reversed core long after pericentre. Deep encounters leave cores spinning above break-up, which shed mass and angular momentum as they settle. Full disruptions approach the canonical fallback law, whereas the late-time slope of partial disruptions is not universal and is set by the debris energy distribution near the surviving core.

papers.title: The Ionospheric Cut-off as a Potential Radio Technosignature
papers.abstract: Radio emission generated on a planetary surface must cross the planet's ionosphere before escaping into space: below the local plasma frequency it is reflected back towards the surface. We investigate this process for broadband radio technosignatures (BRaTs) using a Chapman-layer description of photoionised atmospheres. The plasma frequency depends only weakly on stellar XUV irradiation, scaling as $Q_{\infty}^{1/4}$, implying turnover frequencies of 5-40 MHz for most terrestrial habitable-zone planets, potentially rising towards 100 MHz in extreme environments. The basic signature is simple: the continuum of a surface-origin BRaT should be strongly suppressed below a characteristic frequency that can be estimated from the XUV output of the host star, at every orbital phase and for any viewing geometry. Oblique propagation, magnetic fields, and collisional absorption broaden the cut-off into a smooth escape function, $f_{\mathrm{esc}}(\nu,\phi)$, where $\phi$ is the orbital phase. Because the day-night ionisation pattern is anchored to the substellar point rather than to the rotating surface, disc integration adds a second, more discriminating signature: the half-escape frequency $\nu_{1/2}$ varies predictably (by about 40-50 per cent over the orbit, depending on the angular emission pattern of the leakage) and remains locked to the orbital ephemeris. Finite atmospheric response times introduce modest phase lags but preserve the modulation. A low-frequency turnover alone is not unique to technology, but one that varies periodically with the orbital period would be difficult to reproduce through known astrophysical processes. Although observationally challenging, the ionospheric cut-off is a potential technosignature diagnostic and a novel probe of exoplanet ionospheres.

papers.title: Worldsheet Effective Theory of Abelian-Higgs Cosmic Strings beyond Nambu--Goto
papers.abstract: Cosmic strings can support long-lived excitations confined to their cores, opening channels for energy exchange with the transverse Goldstone modes that describe the string's motion. We derive a covariant worldsheet theory of their coupled dynamics directly from the Abelian-Higgs model at critical coupling, with all interaction coefficients fixed by the microscopic theory. The resulting action, which we validate against numerical lattice field theory simulations, extends the Nambu--Goto description to include a massive scalar shape mode and a massive vector mode. Dualizing the vector reveals a geometric distinction: the shape scalar mode couples to intrinsic worldsheet curvature, while the pseudoscalar couples to normal bundle curvature. These interactions explain the distinct parametric instabilities observed in lattice simulations and predict how the relative polarization of colliding transverse waves controls the excitation of the two internal modes. Our results connect microscopic string structure to the nonlinear worldsheet dynamics, providing a predictive framework for cosmic strings beyond the Nambu--Goto approximation.

papers.title: Fast X-Ray Transients from Dense Circumstellar Material Shock Breakout and Cooling Emission
papers.abstract: In this Letter, we explore the soft X-ray shock breakout (SBO) and cooling emission of supernovae interacting with pre-explosion dense circumstellar material (CSM) shells as a subclass of extragalactic fast X-ray transients. For geometrically thin CSM shells, we find that the SBO luminosities span a range of a few $10^{43}-10^{45}\,{\rm{erg}}\,{\rm{s}}^{-1}$, with peak times typically $\lesssim10^4\,{\rm{s}}$, both of which are primarily determined by the light-travel effect. When the shell's outer radius is located at $\sim100-500\,R_\odot$, the SBO temperatures fall into the energy band covered by the current soft X-ray facilities. We derive analytic lightcurves for SBOs in dense CSM shells and explore how different physical parameters affect the observed lightcurves and the temperature evolution. Despite the multi-temperature nature of the emission caused by the light-travel effect leading to non-thermal-like spectra, we find that the time-resolved spectra within the limited soft X-ray band can still be well described by a blackbody model. This provides a natural explanation for the observed blackbody-like time-resolved spectra of soft X-ray SBO events. Our model can reproduce the observed X-ray lightcurves and temperature evolutions of the three known X-ray SBO events, EP260321a, XRF\,060218, and XRO\,080109, revealing a diversity in the properties of the dense CSM shells ejected by stripped-envelope progenitors before the explosion. Future discoveries of more soft X-ray SBO events by facilities such as Einstein Probe will provide opportunities for probing the episodic mass-loss history of massive stars in the final stages before core collapse.

papers.title: Revisiting Kerr-Newman-(A)dS Black Holes in (f(R)) Gravity: A Kerr-Schild Approach
papers.abstract: It is known that, in the constant-curvature regime, the field equations of $f(R)$ gravity reduce to the Einstein form with an effective cosmological constant, establishing a direct correspondence between stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions in $f(R)$ gravity and their counterparts in general relativity, including the Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Within this framework, we revisit the derivation of these metrics using the Kerr--Schild approach for illustrative purposes. The Maxwell equations are solved independently of the Kerr--Schild function, allowing the electromagnetic source to be determined before addressing the gravitational field equations. We then investigate the possibility of non-constant-curvature solutions, taking quadratic $f(R)$ gravity as a representative model. Remarkably, the field equations within the Kerr--Schild ansatz force the Ricci scalar to be constant, reducing the resulting geometries to the familiar Kerr--Newman--(A)dS family. Thus, our analysis extends the recently established no-go result for uncharged black holes to electrically charged configurations within the framework considered here.

papers.title: Superoutburst Precursors in the Faint SU UMa-type Dwarf Nova KSP-OT-201602a
papers.abstract: We present the discovery and photometric study of an SU UMa-type dwarf nova (DN) KSP-OT-201602a. Korea Microlensing Telescope Network Supernova Program data covered almost four years from 2016 to 2019 in BVI-bands for this field, and discovered this faint SU UMa-type DN. Two superoutbursts (SOs: S1 and S2) and two normal outbursts (NOs: N1 and N2) are observed of which peak brightnesses are V = 18.95 mag (S1), V = 18.69 mag (S2) and V = 19.37 mag (N1), V = 19.11 mag (N2). The phase dispersion minimization analysis on superhump of S1 gives the superhump period of 1.52 hr (= 91.2 minutes = 0.06333 days). The magnitude amplitudes for the SOs are 4.34 mag (S1) and 4.60 mag (S2), and those for the NOs are 3.98 mag (N1) and 4.18 mag (N2). The durations of the SOs are 11.39 days (S1) and 12.00 days (S2), and those for the NOs are 2.68 days (N1) and 3.38 days (N2). Clear evidence of a precursor is identified in S1 before the SO peak and this supports the hypothesis that precursor is an NO triggerring an SO and the superhump, while a potential precursor based on limited data is only observed in S2. While the amplitudes of the SOs appear typical for SU UMa-type DNe, their durations seem to be quite short which might require further model calculations in the future.

papers.title: Spatio-Temporal Evolution of a Steady Transition Region Downflow above a Sunspot
papers.abstract: Super-Sonic Downflows (SSDs) are usually observed above sunspots as redshifted peaks in lower Transition Region (TR) spectral lines and can last from a few minutes to several hours. Utilising high-cadence, $\sim$3 hour long repeated-raster mode observations from Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), we investigate the spatio-temporal dynamics of such a downflow event above NOAA active region 12135. Triple Gaussian fitting to TR spectral lines, along with Non-Force Free Field (NFFF) extrapolation and Differential Emission Measure (DEM) analysis, is performed to study this event. Downflow is initially observed in both the umbral and penumbral regions. Over time, the penumbral downflow fades, while the umbral downflow strengthens and appears as a single structure initially but eventually splits into two spatial segments. The calculated average properties, including downflow speed, electron density, and mass flux for this event, align with established studies. Simultaneous evolution in overlying coronal loops is also observed using imaging data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA). DEM analysis of the coronal emission over the downflow region indicates corresponding changes in cool ($\log_{10}[T/\mathrm{K}] \in [5.5, 5.6]$) coronal plasma. As suggested by recurrent transient brightenings observed in the nearby region in coronal channels and the corresponding fan-spine magnetic topology identified from NFFF extrapolations, magnetic reconnection occurring in this region is proposed to be the cause of this evolution. Our analysis revealed that changes in the morphology of TR downflows are closely associated with evolution of overlying coronal loops.

papers.title: Equation of state of hot and dense QCD at the physical point via the complex Langevin equation
papers.abstract: This study presents the first results for the equation of state of 2+1+1-flavor QCD at the physical point, obtained using the complex Langevin equation. We calculate continuum-extrapolated thermodynamic quantities, such as the baryon density, pressure, the speed of sound and the adiabatic compressibility. The simulations are performed in the isospin-symmetric, strangeness- and charm-neutral setting above the crossover temperature and at unprecedentedly large baryon chemical potentials.

papers.title: Magnolia: a highly magnetized galaxy at redshift $z9$
papers.abstract: The theory of galactic magnetic field growth via dynamo action predicts that the interstellar medium (ISM) of early galaxies would remain virtually unmagnetized on large scales. However, recent observations of strong dust polarization in galaxies at redshifts $z\simeq2.6$ and $z\simeq5.6$ challenge this paradigm. If galaxies indeed host strong, large-scale, coherent magnetic fields at high-$z$, then galaxy evolution and current theories of magnetic field amplification in galaxies should be revisited. To address the full physical complexity of early magnetic field growth in galaxies, we have designed MAGNA SERRA, a suite of radiation-magneto-hydrodynamical (RMHD) cosmological zoom-in simulations with non-equilibrium chemistry. In this first paper from the MAGNA SERRA suite, we present Magnolia, a galaxy hosted in a $\simeq 10^{11}~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ dark matter halo simulated with RAMSES-RT with a $\simeq 10^4~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ mass ($\simeq 10 \,\mathrm{pc}$ spatial) resolution. We find that, at $z\simeq9$, Magnolia has a stellar mass of a few times $10^8~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and is strongly magnetized, reaching a magnetic field of a few $\mu G$ and a plasma beta $\beta\simeq 0.1$ in the densest regions. This strong amplification occurs over a timescale of about 40~Myrs due to the highly dynamical nature of the galaxy, which creates strong compressions and shear. The power spectra of the magnetic and kinetic energies and the spectral energy transfer functions do not suggest dynamo action, but rather an initial magnetic field amplification through a large-scale compression, and a later re-organization of this field from small to large scales. Our findings show that strong galactic magnetization is possible at very high redshifts, which means that magnetic fields can play a dominant role throughout a galaxy's evolutionary history. (abridged)

papers.title: Interpretation of the LZ Event via Inelastic ALP-Dark Photon Transition with Photon Exchange
papers.abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has reported a nuclear recoil event at $248\pm23$~keV with a global significance of about $2.6\sigma$. We for the first time explain it via the inelastic process with photon mediator. We consider a dark matter (DM) axion-like particle (ALP) $a$ converts into a heavier dark photon $\gamma'$ via the nuclear electromagnetic current, and study the photon-mediated endothermic transition $aA\rightarrow\gamma'A$. We derive the kinematics and cross sections for non-relativistic halo and boosted ALPs. A three-bin Poisson fit to the LZ data includes the xenon isotopes, charge form factors, detector efficiency, and energy resolution. Halo DM, which has mass $m\simeq1.2$~TeV, mass splitting $\delta\simeq346$~keV, and near the upper coupling bound, reproduces the event with about $61\%$ in the middle bin. Boosted DM with $v_{0}=0.05\,c$ and $\Phi_{0}=10^{5}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ requires only $m\simeq5.74$~GeV and $\delta\simeq6.66$~MeV to give about $62\%$. We find that a broader Gaussian spread in the incident energy has a significant effect on the fitted masses.

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Bursts from Primordial Black Hole-Induced Neutron Star Collapse
papers.abstract: We show that the capture and subsequent endoparasitic consumption of a neutron star (NS) by a primordial black hole (PBH) can produce a short gamma-ray burst (GRB) without forming an accretion disk. During PBH-induced NS consumption, the NS spin is amplified through angular-momentum conservation and transfer from infalling matter, while flux freezing and a differential-rotation-driven dynamo amplify the magnetic field. We find that, for rapidly rotating millisecond pulsars (MSPs), these mechanisms can power short GRBs through magnetic dipole radiation and magnetic energy release. If asteroid-mass PBHs in the range $10^{-14}M_\odot$--$10^{-11}M_\odot$ constitute the dark matter, we estimate that searches of the Fermi-GBM archive and a future MeV gamma-ray mission such as COSI could detect these bursts. We also discuss possible multimessenger counterparts, including fast radio bursts powered by magnetic energy release, kilonovae and $511\,{\rm keV}$ line emission associated with centrifugally ejected neutron-rich matter, and gravitational waves from the rapid collapse and subsequent black-hole ringdown. Together, these signals probe complementary stages of PBH-induced NS consumption.

papers.title: Majorana dark matter from a thick-to-thin brane junction: Modal stability, real-mediator coannihilation, and a dark-radiation imprint
papers.abstract: We show that the localized spectrum of a $D=7$ thick-to-thin brane junction can host a thermal Majorana dark-matter candidate. The anisotropy of the wall widths isolates a light junction fermion, which a four-dimensional Majorana mass splits into two nearby states. The factorized transverse profiles impose a modal selection rule on all cubic couplings, and together with the relaxation of the softly deformed background this makes the lighter state stable without an imposed dark parity. Because the localized mediator is a real scalar, identical Majorana particles annihilate in the $s$ wave, and the relic coupling becomes nearly independent of the Majorana mass. The junction sector is a Standard-Model singlet whose light chiral mode is a source of dark radiation. Current CMB data restrict its decoupling temperature and imply $0.05\lesssim\dNeff\lesssim0.076$ for dark-matter masses between $10\GeV$ and $1.5\TeV$, a range accessible to next-generation CMB surveys.

papers.title: Resonant Cavity Searches for Millicharged Dark Matter
papers.abstract: A plethora of resonant cavity experiments have been designed to search for ultralight dark matter (DM) candidates, such as axion or dark-photon DM. In this work, we show that these same apparatuses can be sensitive to ultralight millicharged dark matter (mDM) with masses $m_\phi\sim1-100\,\mu\mathrm{eV}$. Similar to axion DM, in the presence of a background magnetic field, mDM acts as an effective current which can excite the modes of a resonant cavity. Importantly, for a cylindrical cavity, axion DM dominantly couples to the transverse magnetic (TM) modes, whereas mDM dominantly couples to the transverse electric (TE) modes. We project the sensitivity to mDM that resonant cavity experiments can achieve if they are able to tune and readout their TE modes. We find that fractional millicharges as small as $\epsilon_m=e_m/e\sim10^{-19}$ can be probed. If mDM constitutes only a subfraction $f_\mDM \lesssim0.2\%$ of the total DM density, competing astrophysical bounds do not apply. In this case, resonant cavities can be the most sensitive probes of mDM in this mass range.

papers.title: Square Kilometre Array Science Data Challenge 3b: EoR inference
papers.abstract: We present and analyse the results of Science Data Challenge 3b (SDC3b; https://sdc3.skao.int/challenges/inference), an Epoch of Reionization (EoR) inference exercise organised by the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) using simulated SKA data. The nine-month challenge, running from October 2024 to May 2025, represents the first community-wide comparison of EoR inference pipelines on common simulated datasets. We consider multiple datasets designed to assess performance on both foreground-free and foreground-contaminated cylindrical power spectra and imaging products, adopting different reionization scenarios and EoR simulation models. We include results from 16 teams, which employ a range of methodologies to infer the posterior distribution of the hydrogen neutral fraction across three redshift intervals spanning z=8.41 to z=6.25. The results show significant inter-team variability of the astrophysical constraints even in the simpler case where only instrumental noise is added to the cosmological signal. This underscores the need for further investigation into the relative contributions of signal modelling, the treatment of instrumental effects, and inference methods to the robustness of the resulting conclusions. Although individual methods can produce biased parameter estimates, the combined average of their estimates remains close to the input values, suggesting that independent approaches can offset method-specific biases.

papers.title: Direct simulation Monte Carlo for dark matter production and phase-space evolution
papers.abstract: To study the early-universe production of dark matter particles beyond thermal equilibrium often requires solving several coupled Boltzmann equations at the phase-space level. We present a new method to address this challenge using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) based on stochastic interactions of an ensemble of particles. We implement and validate efficient algorithms to describe freeze-out, decays, elastic scattering and number-changing processes within the dark sector. These algorithms do not require a discretisation of momentum space on a pre-defined grid and do not rely on approximations such as thermally averaged cross sections. As illustrative example, we consider a scenario with two-step dark matter production, leading to a bimodal phase-space distribution, and consider the subsequent evolution under elastic and number-changing processes. We show that DSMC is a flexible approach to explore out-of-equilibrium processes and solve Boltzmann equations at the phase-space level in order to predict the abundance of dark matter particles and their effect on structure formation.

papers.title: TWIN-2: Timing Solar Radio Bursts between 180-350 MHz Against GOES and Aditya-L1 X-ray Detections
papers.abstract: We have conducted continuous solar observations for approximately two and half years using the Two-Element Interferometer (TWIN) at Gauribidanur Radio Observatory (RRI). During which several solar events have been detected. Our observational period coincides with the maximum events phase of the Solar Cycle 25, providing us opportunity to analyse the evolution of the solar activity. Our analysis of two and half years data show a clear increase in the occurrences of solar events, which is consistent with the expected rise in the solar activity towards the peak phase of the Solar Cycle 25. We further investigate the detected solar radio events using X-ray observations from the space based Aditya-L1 and the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES) satellites. For the automated detection of SRBs, a machine learning suite has been trained. This also serves as an instrument for space weather monitoring. On the 7th of November 2025, a solar storm was detected by our pipeline in realtime. A brief overview of the data-processing pipeline, along with the RFI mitigation techniques employed to identify and characterize the solar events, is also presented. Observation data of two and a half years of TWIN is available for public access. The data has been used in student training programmes on solar radio data analysis, with students carrying out the analysis and contributing to the initial analysis of the detected events.

papers.title: The Universality of Halo Growth and Merger Rates in Modified Gravity Theories
papers.abstract: In the standard $\Lambda$CDM framework, the merger rate of dark matter haloes has been found to follow a nearly universal form, with only weak dependence on halo mass and redshift. We examine whether this universality is preserved in modified gravity (MG) models, where the growth of cosmic structure can deviate from that of general relativity (GR). We use the ELEPHANT suite of large $N$-body simulations to study halo merger rates and mass accretion histories in different modified gravity models, including two representative scenarios beyond-GR: the Hu--Sawicki chameleon $f(R)$ model and the normal branch of the Dvali--Gabadadze--Porrati model. For the mass accretion histories, the modified gravitational effect can produce systematic departures from GR, generally corresponding to more rapid halo growth. The deviations are relatively small when the MG effect is weak, while they become more pronounced in models with strong deviation from GR and can exceed $15\%$ in the extreme case. For the halo merger rate, we find that the nearly universal behavior is well preserved across all the gravity models, with only weak dependence on redshift and halo mass, reflecting the unbiased accretion nature of halo growth. However, apparent deviation from this universality can arise if the halo mass is not defined consistently with the modified gravity model.

papers.title: Dark Matter Model Implications of a Candidate Sub-halo Near the Sun, and the Data Needed to Discriminate Among Them
papers.abstract: Pulsar-timing accelerations point to a localized mass concentration near the Sun, consistent with a dark matter sub-halo. We work out what such an object implies for the nature of dark matter, organizing the implications by their observable effect: suppression or enhancement of structure formation, internal structure and survival after formation, and emission or scattering by the constituents. We discuss ultralight wave dark matter, thermal and nonthermal warm dark matter, dark acoustic oscillations and dark matter-baryon scattering, elastic and inelastic self-interactions, invisible decays with recoil, primordial black holes, indirect detection, and a possible connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy recoil candidate. We then ask what new data would discriminate among these models. The existing accelerations are measured outside the tidal radius, where they are blind to the interior mass distribution, to the object's velocity, and to the sub-halo population. We identify four routes that lift these degeneracies: accelerations measured inside the halo, which separate point-mass, cuspy, and cored profiles; lensing and accretion, which test whether the mass is compact; the morphology of annihilation or decay emission, which probes the inner profile; and a search for a comoving stellar population, which tests whether the object is dark and measures its velocity. We also contrast this program with pulsar-timing-array searches for transiting dark matter substructure, which probe vastly lighter objects through a different observable.

papers.title: The Cosmic Infrared Background from Population III.1 Supermassive Stars and Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmic infrared background (CIB) that is expected to arise from the Population (Pop) III.1 supermassive black hole (SMBH) formation scenario, which involves early SMBH seeding via supermassive primordial star formation enabled by dark matter annihilation heating. We model the emission from Pop III.1 supermassive stars, including their growth phase, flash ionization phase, and early black hole accretion phase, as well as accompanying emission from lower-mass Pop III.2 stars. The CIB is composed of stellar and SMBH accretion disk continuum radiation, nebular continuum emission, and Ly$\alpha$ radiation redistributed through scattering in the neutral intergalactic medium. Based on the feedback regulated Pop III.1 model of Petkova et al. (2026), our fiducial model assumes $\sim 10^5\,M_\odot$ Pop III.1 stars forming by $z_{\rm flash}=20$ with a comoving number density of $\sim0.2\,{\rm cMpc}^{-3}$. For this model, the combined stellar contribution is less than $1\%$ of existing direct and diffuse CIB measurements. However, the contribution to the CIB from $z\sim6-20$ SMBH accretion is expected to be larger than the Pop III.1 stellar component for average Eddington ratios $\lambda_{\text{Edd}} \sim 0.01$. Latest CIB observations place constraints of $\lambda_{\text{Edd}} \lesssim 0.3$ for the fiducial Pop III.1 model during these epochs.

papers.title: Design and Forecasts for a Rubin Twilight Program for Nearby Type Ia Supernovae
papers.abstract: Nearby Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) are important for supernova cosmology, but saturation in 30 s exposures, gaps in light-curve sampling, and the footprint of Vera C. Rubin Observatory's baseline Wide-Fast-Deep (WFD) survey limit the nearby sample. To improve the low-$z$ sample, we propose a twilight follow-up program using Rubin Observatory for 1-5 s griz exposures at solar altitudes $-12^\circ \le \mathrm{Alt}_\odot \le -9^\circ$. Using simulations of one year of WFD observations, we find that twilight follow-up adds 230 quality-selected SNe Ia from an external sample drawn primarily from the Transient Name Server (TNS). At $z<0.08$, the usable sample increases from 368 to 643 SNe Ia, including 50 WFD events recovered by refitting their light curves with twilight photometry. Combining these twilight observations with high-redshift WFD and Deep Drilling Field samples increases the statistical-only dark-energy $(w_0,w_a)$ figure of merit from 49.3 to 58.3 (18%) and reduces $\sigma(w_a)$ by 10%. For measurements of structure growth at $0.02 \le z<0.06$, the fractional uncertainty on $f\sigma_8$ decreases from 0.783 to 0.305. Restricting the program to $-12^\circ \le \mathrm{Alt}_\odot \le -11^\circ$ reduces the dark-energy improvement to 7.2%. These short exposures could also provide unsaturated photometry of potential distance-ladder calibrators at $z<0.02$.
authors: the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration

papers.title: First $_ m-w$ Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
papers.abstract: Though fast radio bursts (FRBs) are widely advocated as a dark energy probe, no valid $\Omega_m-w$ constraint has been obtained exclusively from FRB data to date. Benefiting from a rapidly growing localized sample and a novel statistical framework for modeling the dispersion measure (DM), we report the first simultaneous inference of the matter density $\Omega_m$ and dark energy equation of state parameter $w$ from FRBs alone, without external observational priors on these two parameters. We combine a multi-parameter emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum with a physically motivated electron prescription to construct a cosmology-dependent cosmic-DM distribution. Within this unified analysis framework, the mean and variance of DM respond self-consistently to the same underlying cosmology, directly connecting the FRB likelihood to both cosmic expansion and structure growth. Analyzing 125 localized FRBs at $0.105\leq z\leq2.148$, we obtain $\Omega_m = 0.33^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ and $w = -0.80^{+0.28}_{-0.38}$ under the flat $w$CDM model. We find a new positive $\Omega_m-w$ degeneracy in the FRB posterior, opposite to the strong anticorrelation derived from Type Ia supernovae, offering a complementary test of dark energy properties and highlighting their potential in future precision cosmological studies.

papers.title: 3D Binary Evolution of a Merging Binary Black Hole Progenitor
papers.abstract: Mass transfer is a highly dynamical 3D process that spans evolutionary timescales in binary stars. It is key to the production of gravitational waves through formation of binary black holes and other double compact objects. We integrate global 3D hydrodynamics into stellar evolutionary modeling to resolve mass transfer across nuclear timescales. We employ the shellular approximation in the stellar evolution code MESA to map a 3D spatial structure by equipotential shells in the Roche geometry to maintain hydrostatic equilibrium across tidally-distorted surfaces. We employ the method of time-incremented multiscale evolution to alternate between stellar evolution and 3D hydrodynamics to span large timescales with dynamical feedback. We employ this framework to examine a likely merging binary black hole progenitor system of a low-metallicity 30Msol donor star and 9.3Msol black hole from the end of the main sequence to core Carbon depletion. We modeled two complete mass transfer phases in 3D while self-consistently accounting for stellar evolution. These comprised a thermal-timescale early Case B phase and a nuclear-timescale late Case B phase. The prescription of Kolb & Ritter (1990) closely predicted the results of 3D evolution, except at the end of the first phase of mass transfer; our 3D model remained well-contained by the outer Lagrange point, despite 1D predictions of substantial L3 overflow during this stage. We find incorporating 3D hydrodynamics during Case B mass transfer did not significantly impact expected merger times. Our model never overflowed L3 as predicted by 1D prescriptions. L2/L3 outflows formed even while underflowing those equipotentials. Our model suggests these outflows can be neglected for the evolution of similar systems, but were dense enough to potentially impact X-ray observations.

papers.title: Transition Zone from ExoEarth to ExoVenus: Critical Insight from Planets on the Edge
papers.abstract: Venus and Earth, planets with similar masses and radii, provide astonishingly different environments, raising the question of why these two rocky worlds evolved so differently. Explaining this divergence is a central challenge in comparative planetology and astrobiology. Now, atmospheric studies of exoplanets can explore the possibilities of terrestrial planet evolution, especially in the era of JWST; however, we have not yet realized the critical insights rocky exoplanets in the Transition Zone (TZ) can provide. These TZ planets in the overlap between the Habitable Zone and Venus Zone can test how incident stellar irradiation affects surface water retention and habitability. Observations of exoplanets in the TZ can probe not only the emergence and decline of exoplanet habitability but also test hypotheses about Venus' past, complementing upcoming Venus flagship missions. Here, we analyze NASA's Exoplanet Archive, updated with Gaia DR3 data, and provide a target list of 23 rocky exoplanets in the Earth-to-Venus Transition Zone, along with 2 planets in the Venus Evolution Zone (EV). We examine their demographics and quantify their potential for follow-up observations. This list of rocky TZ and EV planets allows observers to optimize target selection and observing strategy for specific instruments. Characterizing exoplanets in the Transition Zone will be critical to investigating open questions about the emergence and decline of habitability on rocky worlds, the evolution from an exo-Earth to an exo-Venus, and Earth's future.

papers.title: The SPACE Program IV: Atmospheric Features on the Cold Transiting Sub-Neptune TOI-6478 b
papers.abstract: Among the current population of exoplanets there are very few sub-Neptunes that have their atmospheric composition identified. This is primarily due to sub-Neptunes having high metallicity, clouds, and/or hazes obscuring absorption features. This often produces a spectrum that presents itself as a featureless spectrum especially in the near-IR. However, there are tentative trends that suggest sub-Neptunes with the lowest equilibrium temperatures ($\mathrm{T_{eq} < 400\:K}$) have detectable features, perhaps due to inefficient haze production or cloud sedimentation. TOI-6478 b is a low-density sub-Neptune exoplanet ($\rm <\mathrm{9.9\:M_{\oplus}}$ and $\rm \sim 4.5R_{\oplus}$) with an equilibrium temperature $\mathrm{T_{eq} = 220 \:K}$ assuming zero albedo. In this study, we present the highest S/N spectral feature ($\sim$6) of any sub-Neptune detected using HST/WFC3. We detect this spectral feature using a robust analysis that incorporates the Transit Light Source Effect (TLSE) to rule out false detections due to stellar activity. With the narrow bandpass of HST we were unable to distinguish whether the spectral feature at 1.4$\mu$m is from H$_2$O or CH$_4$ absorption. Meanwhile, self-consistent atmospheric models provide physical motivation for CH$_4$ to be the dominant absorber given that H$_2$O should condense or cold trap at higher pressures. Through our analysis we determine that HST/WFC3 alone cannot distinguish between major absorbers. However, a broader wavelength coverage by JWST will be able to measure the atmospheric composition in detail, due to the high S/N features for this target.

papers.title: Strong Coupling of Cosmological Perturbations in mLQC-I: The Hybrid Approach
papers.abstract: We study nonlinear perturbative consistency of scalar perturbations in modified loop quantum cosmology I (mLQC-I) within the hybrid approach. We express the quadratic and cubic Hamiltonians in a common canonical representation before imposing the background constraint and adopt a minimal sector-preserving cubic regularization. Near the pre-bounce quantum-geometrical de Sitter phase, nonlinear coefficients become strongly enhanced. The $\alpha_I^3/\kappa$ term survives the leading ultraviolet cubic kernel for fixed nondegenerate triangles in the selected frequency assignment. This enhancement occurs in four inflationary potentials, with formal suppression scales sensitive to their normalization. In an assumed factorized quartic continuation, a selected lapse contact does not cancel enhanced cubic exchange in an analytic scattering family. However, the derived quartic Legendre contribution cancels that lapse contact at $V=K_\phi$ in the Hamiltonian. The full amplitude remains unresolved: omitted quartic sectors are not proved subleading, and the formal scales do not determine a physical cutoff. For an instantaneous quadratic state initialized at the bounce, the equilateral cubic diagnostic first reaches unity at $K\simeq0.6483m_{\rm P}$. Evolution over $0\le t/t_{\rm P}\le10$ lowers this crossing to $K\simeq0.64626m_{\rm P}$. Sampled shape and independent frequency-assignment tests do not lower these thresholds. A fourth-order adiabatic ultraviolet tail can be attached without changing the tested finite modes. These results identify pre-bounce nonlinear enhancement and a candidate bounce-state window. Broader evolution and shape tests, renormalized backreaction, observational mode mapping on a consistently normalized background, and a complete fourth-order theory remain necessary to establish interacting consistency.

papers.title: Kinetic Tomography with Diffuse Interstellar Bands in APOGEE DR17
papers.abstract: Context: Mapping gas flows in the interstellar medium is key to understanding the formation of structure in our Milky Way. Methods that simultaneously reconstruct clouds' distances and line-of-sight velocities are called kinetic tomography (KT). Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are powerful tracers for such maps because they trace the integrated dust density and the dust-weighted velocity. Previous DIB-KT works had small samples with coarse kpc-scale resolution and could not capture vertical disk structure. Aims: Make 4D (3D position + radial velocity) maps of the Milky Way from new, high-quality 15,273 {\AA} DIB detections in APOGEE DR17. Methods: We combine variational inference and Gaussian processes with a mixture likelihood for low signal-to-noise detections and marginalization over distance uncertainties. We calibrate the model on mock fields and spectral injection tests and validate the map against independent tracers of the dust density (3D dust maps) and velocity substructure (masers and young stellar clusters). Results: We recover a posterior distribution over 3D maps of the density and velocity structure of the 15,273 {\AA} DIB within 6 kpc of the Sun. We measure the large-scale structure of the DIB disk (scale length, height and flare) and detect vertical distortions consistent with the warp. On smaller scales, the map resolves distance ambiguities in gas longitude-velocity diagrams. From the second-order velocity structure function, we measure a slope (0.64 $\pm$ 0.04) consistent with Kolmogorov turbulence, amplitude consistent with expectations for molecular clouds, and a preliminary ratio of compressive-to-solenoidal modes. Conclusions: With larger DIB catalogs expected from SDSS-V, this framework should resolve kinematic substructure at the scales needed to constrain the formation and dynamics of individual clouds and voids. (abridged)

papers.title: EuclidFM: Foundation Model for Compact Photometric Survey Representation
papers.abstract: We present EuclidFM, a compact self-supervised model that learns object-level representations from heterogeneous catalogue photometry in Euclid Quick Data Release 1. Using 90,258 sources across three Euclid Deep Fields, a masked-autoencoder Transformer reconstructs withheld fluxes and uncertainties from available measurements, producing a 128-dimensional embedding per source. The embeddings encode morphological and photometric information: sources with high point-like probability have, on average, 12.4 similarly classified neighbours among their 15 nearest neighbours, compared with 4.3 under field- and magnitude-stratified randomization. Linear models trained on frozen embeddings predict VIS magnitudes with correlations of 0.954-0.980 across three held-out fields. For sources with VIS aperture-flux uncertainties up to 1 microJy, incorporating embeddings reduces the root-mean-square error in predicted log uncertainty by at least 24% relative to a magnitude-only model. A classifier trained on spectroscopically confirmed sources identifies 1,150 quasar candidates, but only 21 of the 156 candidates with accepted external counterparts show AGN evidence, including 12 spectroscopic quasars. The classifier's transferability to the wider photometric catalogue therefore remains uncertain, and its purity and completeness require further evaluation. Independently of classification, EuclidFM provides a common representation for downstream survey analyses when photometric coverage differs between sources. Code and data are available at https://github.com/AI-Driven-HEP/EuclidFM.

papers.title: Validation and Physical Characterization of Seven TESS Exoplanets: A Compact Multi-Planet System and Targets for Atmospheric Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) continues to identify thousands of transit candidates that require statistical validation to rule out astrophysical false positives before atmospheric characterization can be pursued. We statistically validate and characterize seven TESS exoplanet candidates orbiting five host stars. As a consistency check of our automated vetting and Bayesian inference pipeline, we include TOI-2392.03, a sub-Neptune companion previously validated in the literature. Our framework combines automated signal retrieval, pixel-level centroid and Gaia DR3 contamination analysis, and false positive probability (FPP) computation with the TRICERATOPS vetting engine. Physical and orbital parameters are derived via nested sampling (juliet/Dynesty), complemented by an empirical mass-radius relation, since no dynamical mass measurements are available. Applying the same procedure to all candidates, we statistically validate six new exoplanets ($\mathrm{FPP} < 0.015$ and $\mathrm{NFPP} < 0.001$), one of which (TOI-7721.01) lies close to the FPP threshold. We report the period ratios of the three-planet system TOI-2392, and identify TOI-7721.01 and TOI-1277.02 as the candidates with the highest Transmission Spectroscopy Metrics (TSM) in our sample, making them targets of interest for atmospheric follow-up with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the upcoming Ariel mission.

papers.title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
papers.abstract: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate. Given that standard stellar evolution is not able to produce subsolar candidates, a confident detection would point either to new physics or to unconventional astrophysical pathways. These include collapsars, where the outer parts of neutrino-cooled accretion disks around newborn stellar-mass black holes are subject to fragmentation and give rise to subsolar neutron stars, which can later merge with the central black hole. We show that current subsolar searches may miss a significant fraction of these neutron star-black hole mergers, because their templates do not account for the small mass ratios, the tidal disruption of the neutron star, and the effects of the surrounding gas. This result motivates improving the waveform modeling used in current subsolar searches and building adequate template banks tailored to these systems.

papers.title: Twisted resonant orbits: Quantifying the deceleration of the Galactic bar
papers.abstract: Recent structural discoveries in Gaia Data Release 3 reveal distinct, chevron-shaped over-densities in the radial phase space of the halo. Although initial interpretations identify these features as the phase-mixed relics of a past galaxy merger, their prominent asymmetry and persistence at high metallicities strongly challenge this interpretation. These features are better explained as a dynamical response to a Galactic bar, where stars are trapped in resonances. We establish the fractional $v_r$ asymmetry of the chevrons as a quantitative diagnostic tool for the bar's rotational state. We utilise test-particle simulations of a Milky Way-like galaxy to model various bar pattern speed evolutions, including decelerating and constant speed scenarios. By mapping the fractional asymmetry of the phase-space chevrons across a parameter space of bar deceleration rates and pattern speeds, we establish a direct correlation between the bar's deceleration and the rotational response of the resonant orbits. Comparing these simulated constraints with observational data from Gaia DR3 provides a framework for measuring the current deceleration of the Galactic bar, and a probe of the amount of dynamical friction occurring between the baryonic and dark matter content of the Milky Way. We find a dimensionless deceleration parameter $\eta \equiv - \dot{\Omega}_b/\Omega_b^2 = 0.0015^{+0.0016}_{-0.0009}$, equivalent to $\dot{\Omega}_b = -2.23^{+1.50}_{-2.46} \, \text{km s}^{-1} \text{kpc}^{-1} \text{Gyr}^{-1}$, in agreement with previous estimates obtained with independent methods. Gaia DR4 should sharpen this measurement considerably.

papers.title: Simulation-based inference for gravitational-wave cosmology: parameter reconstruction of a first-order electroweak phase transition
papers.abstract: The detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from a cosmological first- order phase transition would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model, with a strong electroweak phase transition (EWPT) at LISA as a prime example. Reconstructing the underlying model from such a signal is challenging, since the map from the model parameters to the spectrum is degenerate and strong transitions occupy only small and sparse regions of parameter space. We show that simulation-based inference (SBI), a likelihood-free approach applicable to generic SGWB sources, provides a reliable parameter reconstruction despite these difficulties. We first apply SBI to the thermodynamic parameters characterizing the transition, namely its strength, inverse duration, temperature and bubble wall velocity. As a concrete application, we then consider a strong EWPT in a singlet extension of the Standard Model and reconstruct the model parameters from the resulting SGWB. We find that the SBI posteriors agree with those of a likelihood-based Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis, at negligible cost per data set once the network has been trained. Using the network posterior as the proposal for importance sampling with the exact likelihood further corrects its remaining deviations, at a sampling efficiency several orders of magnitude higher than sampling from the prior. SBI thus offers a fast and flexible framework for the cosmological science case of LISA

papers.title: Top-heavy Initial Mass Functions are not enough at cosmic dawn
papers.abstract: A top-heavy stellar initial mass function (IMF) has been proposed to explain the unexpected abundance of ultraviolet (UV)-bright galaxies at cosmic dawn. We test this possibility using the metallicity-dependent, top-heavy IMF recently proposed by Chon et al. (2024), which is motivated by simulations of metal-poor star formation. We compare this IMF with a Salpeter IMF, self-consistently including the associated changes in UV emission, supernova feedback, metal enrichment, and dust production. At fixed star formation rate, the Chon IMF enhances the intrinsic UV luminosity by a factor ${B}_{1500}\simeq4.7$-$2.8$ over halo masses $M_h=10^{8-12}\,M_\odot$. However, its larger supernova rate suppresses star formation and increases dust attenuation, reducing the net boost to ${B}_{\rm UV}\simeq2.0$-$1.06$. For halos relevant to the bright end of the UV luminosity function, the enhancement is only ${B}_{\rm UV}\simeq1.2$-$1.4$, or about $0.3$ mag. Calculations with the DELPHI semi-analytic model confirm that the self-consistent Chon and Salpeter UV luminosity functions differ by less than $0.5$ dex at $z\simeq11$-$17$. Thus, a top-heavy IMF alone cannot explain the bright galaxy excess. Conversely, the predicted pair-instability supernova abundance differs by factors of $2$-$6$ between the two IMFs, providing a potentially cleaner observational diagnostic of the high-mass stellar populations at these early epochs.

papers.title: Theory of Particle Scattering on Superconducting Qubits: From Single Devices to Quantum Arrays
papers.abstract: Superconducting qubits provide microwave-scale transitions and thus offer quantum targets for direct particle scattering with extremely small energy transfer. We develop a general framework for inelastic scattering in which an incident particle exchanges an off-shell photon with a superconducting quantum circuit, inducing a transition from a lower-energy internal state of the circuit to a higher-energy one. The target dependence is encoded in a finite-momentum electromagnetic transition current and, for charge-dominated response, in a qubit transition form factor. A key feature of particle scattering is that a microwave-scale excitation does not necessarily correspond to a long-wavelength interaction, since nonrelativistic particles can transfer spatial momenta much larger than the deposited energy. The full finite-momentum device response is therefore essential. We specialize the formalism to transmon qubits, construct a realistic electrostatic response for a planar Xmon-style transmon, and apply it to photon-mediated scattering of eV-scale bosonic dark matter, including final-state Bose stimulation. We find that the resulting enhancement substantially improves the projected sensitivity at the lowest masses. Owing to the exceptionally low transition threshold of superconducting qubits, this approach opens sensitivity to dark matter in the eV-to-keV mass range, which remains largely unexplored by existing direct-detection experiments. We further show that $N$ independently operated qubits give the expected rate proportional to $N$, while suitably prepared Dicke states can in principle achieve a collective enhancement approaching $N^2$ when spatial coherence is maintained across the array. These results establish superconducting qubits as quantum targets for direct particle scattering and provide a framework for optimizing low-threshold dark-matter searches.

papers.title: Testing the Universality of RAR Model with Constraints on Fermionic Dark Matter for M31
papers.abstract: The Ruffini--Arg\"uelles--Rueda (RAR) model describes dark matter as a self-gravitating system of massive fermions in thermodynamic equilibrium within general relativity. It suggests a dual morphology in galaxies: a highly degenerate quantum core mimicking a central supermassive black hole, and a classical halo that explains galactic rotation curves. Earlier applications of the model to the Milky Way restricted the fermion mass to $mc^{2}=48\text{--}345~\text{keV}$, and the orbits of the S-stars around Sagittarius~A$^{\ast}$ (Sgr~A$^{\ast}$) favored $mc^{2}=56~\text{keV}$, whereas a recent thermodynamic stability analysis allows only $mc^{2}\approx194\text{--}387~\text{keV}$. In this work, we apply the RAR model to the Andromeda galaxy (M31), which hosts a dark compact object of approximately $1.4\times10^{8}~M_{\odot}$ within $0.19~\text{pc}$, roughly 33 times the mass of Sgr~A$^{\ast}$. We solve the relativistic equilibrium equations for $mc^{2}=6\text{--}60~\text{keV}$. For all these masses, the fermionic core lies within $0.19~\text{pc}$ and provides the central mass without a black hole. With a bulge and disk added, the total rotation curve is statistically acceptable ($\chi^{2}/N_{\text{dof}}\approx1.18$) but lies below the disk data at $3\text{--}11~\text{kpc}$, an offset attributed to the baryonic models we adopted. The Navarro--Frenk--White (NFW) and Burkert profiles fitted to the same data give a lower $\chi^{2}$ but require an additional black hole. The stability of the M31 core against gravitational collapse limits the fermion mass to $mc^{2}\lesssim60~\text{keV}$. With the earlier Milky Way range, a single fermion can therefore describe both galaxies only for $mc^{2}=48\text{--}60~\text{keV}$, which includes $56~\text{keV}$. With the thermodynamic range, no fermionic core can supply the central mass of M31, so M31 would have to host a black hole.

papers.title: Orbital dynamics and gravitational wave of Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter
papers.abstract: The dynamical properties of bound particle orbits around a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) are investigated. An analysis of the horizon topology shows that both event and cosmological horizons emerge within specific parametric regimes. Curvature invariants, including the Ricci scalar, Ricci-squared, and Kretschmann scalar, confirm the existence of a curvature singularity at $r = 0$. By utilizing the pericenter precession data of the S2 star in Sgr A*, the PFDM parameter is constrained to $0 < \lambda < 7.726412 \times 10^{5}$ M$_{\odot}$. For a source moving along a periodic orbit, the emitted gravitational waveforms exhibit two key features: (i) the orbital period increases with the ``zoom'' number, accompanied by a modest growth in wave amplitude, and (ii) the PFDM parameter nonlinearly modulates the period, leading to a slight amplitude suppression and introducing only a negligible phase shift relative to the vacuum case. These results explicitly characterize the local imprints of PFDM on relativistic orbital dynamics and offer predictions that are testable by future high-precision astrometric and gravitational-wave observations.

papers.title: Traversable wormholes from entropy-corrected holographic dark energy with quasinormal mode stability in $f(R,T)$ gravity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate holographic dark energy (HDE) motivated energy density profiles as viable matter sources for the construction of traversable wormholes in the framework of $f(R,T)$ gravity. Wormhole solutions are developed using entropy-corrected HDE models based on the Bekenstein--Hawking, R\'enyi, and Moradpour formalisms. We derive the corresponding shape functions and analyze the influence of the model parameters on the flare-out conditions, obtaining the parameter bounds required for traversability. The null energy condition is examined under these constraints and is found to be violated near the wormhole throat, thereby providing the exotic matter content necessary to sustain the geometry. We further evaluate the total gravitational energy and the complexity factor, showing that the internal structure of the wormhole spacetime is highly sensitive to the underlying entropy prescription. The regularity of the solutions is tested through curvature invariants, confirming the absence of curvature singularities and the asymptotic decay of the Kretschmann scalar. In addition, the generalized Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equation is used to study hydrostatic equilibrium, where the inward hydrostatic force is balanced by the anisotropic force and the extra force induced by the matter--geometry coupling. Finally, scalar and electromagnetic quasinormal modes are computed using the third-order WKB approximation. The negative imaginary parts of all obtained frequencies indicate damped oscillations and hence perturbative stability of the wormhole configurations. Our results show that entropy-corrected HDE models, particularly the R\'enyi and Moradpour cases, significantly affect the curvature profile, structural complexity, equilibrium behavior, and ringdown response of traversable wormholes in modified $f(R,T)$ gravity.

papers.title: Damour--Solodukhin Wormholes: Matter Sources, Observational Constraints, and Accretion Dynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate the physical realization and observational properties of Damour--Solodukhin wormholes within general relativity. We first construct an explicit matter source supporting this geometry, consisting of a phantom scalar field coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, and examine both electric and magnetic configurations. We then study the propagation of photons and derive constraints on the wormhole deformation parameter $\lambda$ using Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr A*. We show that, for $\lambda^2 \leq 1/2$, the shadow radius coincides exactly with the Schwarzschild value, although the radial geometry continues to affect gravitational lensing and the structure of photon rings. Using a thin accretion disk with a Johnson SU emissivity profile, we investigate the resulting optical images and examine the effects of the wormhole throat on their structure. Finally, we analyze stationary relativistic accretion and demonstrate that, for identical boundary conditions, the energy density and particle number density are independent of $\lambda$ throughout the common exterior region, while the radial velocity retains an explicit dependence on the deformation parameter. We also derive the condition $0 < w < (1+4\lambda^2)^{-1}$ for the existence of an exterior sonic point. These results highlight the observational degeneracy between Damour--Solodukhin wormholes and Schwarzschild black holes in the small-deformation regime, while identifying the geometric and dynamical effects through which this degeneracy may be investigated.

papers.title: Probing the Graviton Mass through the Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background Last-Scattering Surface
papers.abstract: A nonzero graviton mass makes gravitational waves of different momenta travel different distances during the same cosmic interval. A relic stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) with a finite momentum bandwidth therefore samples a shell of finite thickness, rather than the thin source shell of massless propagation from a single epoch. We describe this effective last-scattering surface by mapping the momentum and emission-time distribution into a radial visibility window in an FLRW background. The calculation uses the geometric-optics propagation relation and includes both dispersion and finite emission duration, without a small-mass or narrow-band approximation. We then calculate how radial averaging changes the angular power for an early-produced background whose momentum channels trace a common source-fluctuation field. For a scale-invariant source spectrum, moving a thin shell leaves its angular power unchanged, so the reduction in power isolates the effect of its finite thickness. For a logarithmic momentum width of $0.5$, mass-to-momentum ratios $q=0.3,1,3$ give angular-power ratios of approximately $0.974$, $0.771$, and $0.508$ at $\ell=10$. At a representative frequency of $3\,\mathrm{nHz}$, these ratios correspond to masses of approximately $3.6\times10^{-24}$--$1.2\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}$. We establish a framework that maps the graviton mass to the SGWB angular power spectrum through its effect on propagation distances and the radial window, for a specified source distribution and frequency selection. Using this framework for graviton-mass inference requires a source and detector model; the calculation here establishes the angular response rather than an observational sensitivity.
